title: Quickstart Visual Sanitizer: Tokenized Overlays, Theming, and Locale-safe Crops
creator: Marina Cortez
description:
Problem:
We need a repeatable, brand-consistent pipeline for generating quickstart and docs screenshots that are safe for release across regions and customers. Current ad-hoc screenshot assets suffer from: inconsistent accent colors, accidental display of identifiable customer data in examples, hard-to-localize crops (UI strings get cut off), and manual rework each release.

Goal:
Deliver a design-driven screenshot sanitizer and templating workflow that produces:
- Tokenized overlays for sensitive fields (email, API keys, org names) with adjustable privacy levels.
- Brand theming layer (accent/color tokens, font scale presets) so screenshots match marketing and console palettes automatically.
- Locale-aware safe-crop rules and micro-layouts to avoid truncation in languages with longer strings.
- Lightweight masking presets (blur, placeholder text, tokenized hash) and export formats for all release channels (docs, console, marketplace).

Scope & Deliverables:
1) Design system tokens & presets: standard accent palettes, CTA highlights, input field states, and compact/regular screenshot sizes.
2) Sanitizer ruleset: regex + heuristic detection for PII (emails, UUIDs, API-like keys), with default transformation rules (tokenize->"[redacted-token-01]", mask->blur, placeholder->"example@company.com").
3) Overlay components in Figma: masked pill, hashed token pill, blurred input component, and a chrome-level header/footer that stays brand-safe.
4) Localization-safe crop guidelines: per-component safe margins, dynamic width previews for selected locales (en, de, ja, fr, es).
5) Export automation doc: step-by-step for content authors and engineering (CLI + script snippets) and a reference screenshot generation checklist.

Trade-offs & decisions to validate:
- Tokenized placeholders vs realistic-looking synthetic data: tokenized placeholders are safer but less relatable in marketing; we propose tokenized placeholders for docs and synthetic examples for marketing with a review gate.
- Aggressive auto-detection of PII could over-mask system strings (e.g., model hashes) — include whitelist heuristics per component.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Designers can produce a release screenshot in <= 12 minutes following the guide.
- Automated sanitizer catches 95% of seeded PII test cases in sample page exports.
- Screenshots pass localization checks for the 5 priority locales without manual cropping.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (design + prototypes): deliver Figma components and rulebook (this ticket).
- Phase 2 (implementation): handoff to SDK/eng for an internal screenshot CLI that applies tokenization and crops; integration with marketing/docs pipelines.
- Phase 3 (validation): run a release dry-run on next minor release assets and fix gaps.

Metrics & risk:
- Track average time to produce a screenshot and number of manual edits post-export.
- Risk: false positives in sanitizer will create extra review work. Mitigation: whitelist config per template and a "preview raw" toggle for reviewers.
acceptance_criteria: Figma component library with 6 sanitized overlay variants (token, blur, placeholder, pill, hashed, hidden)
Written sanitizer rulebook with examples and whitelist instructions
Localization-safe crop guide with margin specs for EN/DE/FR/ES/JA
Export checklist and sample CLI snippet documented in the repo
Measure: sanitizer test suite meets >=95% detection on seeded PII dataset
